name: IconLibrary
description: Rules for the system's icon library (Lucide): which icons exist, what they are called, how they are drawn and how they are brought into Figma. It is not a component: what is painted on screen is Icon.

dos: Look the icon up in icons/catalog.json (all of Lucide) by name, tags or category. If you cannot find it by name, search by tags: "borrar" does not exist, but "delete" does.
To use it in code, first add it to icons/registry.json with its `use` field. The catalog is what exists; the registry is what is approved.
In Figma, change a component's icon by instance swap with the "Category / name" component; do not draw it by hand or paste loose SVGs.
One icon, one meaning: do not use the same icon for two different actions on the same screen.

donts.case: Using a Lucide icon that is not in icons/registry.json
donts.useInstead: Add it to the registry (with its `use`) and regenerate icons.ts
donts.why: The closed list avoids duplicate or contradictory icons and keeps the bundle small.

donts.case: Mixing icons from another library with Lucide ones
donts.why: Each library has its own stroke, rounding and grid; mixing them is noticeable.

donts.case: A lone icon, with no text, for something important
donts.useInstead: Icon plus text, or IconButton with aria-label
donts.why: The meaning of a lone icon is not universal and a screen reader does not announce it.

donts.case: Resizing or recoloring the icon by hand inside a component
donts.useInstead: The size and color of the parent component (Button, IconButton, TextField)
donts.why: The parent already sets them with tokens; a local adjustment breaks consistency.

related.difference: Icon draws an icon from this library on screen with size and accessibility.
Button whose only content is an icon; requires aria-label.
Phosphor library: 16 px grid, filled shapes and regular / fill weights. One of the two is chosen per project.

props.name: name
props.description: Icon name in kebab-case, as it appears in icons/catalog.json (`arrow-right`). In code, the same name in PascalCase (`ArrowRight`). In Figma, the "Category / arrow-right" component.

root.description: 24 × 24 canvas with the icon's strokes. No fill: stroke only.

stroke.description: Icon strokes. Color inherited from the text (currentColor in code; color variable in Figma).

a11y.role: None by default: decorative (aria-hidden). With `label`, role="img" and aria-label.
a11y.name: Provided by the Icon component (label prop), not by the library.
a11y.focusIndicator: Does not receive focus: not interactive.
a11y.minTarget: Does not apply to the icon; if it is inside a button, the press target is the button's.
a11y.contrastNote: An icon with meaning needs ≥ 3:1 against the background (WCAG 1.4.11). It inherits the parent's color: check it there.

canvas.note: All Lucide icons are drawn at 24 × 24 with a 2 px stroke, with rounded caps and joins.

renderSizes.note: Set by the parent component (see Icon.contract.json). The 24 × 24 is scaled; when reduced, the stroke thins proportionally.

catalog.rule: Never edited by hand. To update to a new Lucide version: `npm run icons:catalog -- --update`.

registry.rule: Subset of the catalog approved for code. check.mjs fails if a registry name does not exist in the catalog and warns if it is an old alias.

figma.componentName: Main category title / name in kebab-case
figma.componentDescription: First line `lucide:name` (used to recognize and avoid duplicates); then categories and tags, so Figma's search finds them.
figma.idempotent: Repeating a batch does not duplicate: it skips icons that already exist.

needsReview: The Figma code (scripts/build-figma-icons.mjs) was tested against a simulation of the API, not in a real file. Test first with `npm run icons:figma` (the registry icons) before running --all.
The stroke variable (colors.neutral.neutral.12) is an assumption: the real name in Figma may be different. If it is not found, strokes stay black and the script warns about it.
The main category is the first one Lucide lists for each icon; many icons have several. The full list goes in the component description.
The stroke thins when scaled to 14–20 px (at 16 px it goes from 2 to 1.33). If this is not liked, decide on a fixed stroke per size; Lucide allows it in code (absoluteStrokeWidth).
Some registry names may be old Lucide aliases (Trash2 → Trash): they still work, but check.mjs warns about it.
The registry icons' uses (`use`) are guidance; they do not come from Lucide.
